tips.comment: Lost by just a neck last time at Yarmouth, and the top yard is sure to have placed him well to gain compensation today.

She finished 3rd on debut at Yarmouth on good 15 days ago when raced green into the 7f trip but got the hang of it later on & was only beaten 1L. She should be wiser today for that experience & trainer C.Appleby has good record with novice & maiden 2 & 3year olds at both Rowley Mile & here at July Course & won this race in 2023 .

Romeo Montague finished 7th while on racecourse bow at York in a novice race. The form of that race seems solid enough for this one, and the booking of Ryan adds another layer of trust for the selection's follow-up race.
Those at the front of the betting might be susceptible to one of the newcomers. This one from the Hyam stable might be the answer. Bred to be quick at two and will have been well-schooled.

Glittering Show is a 2-year-old colt trained by Marco Botti (153 2-year-old winners since 2012). He is a full brother to Swift Asset, a 2-year-old winner for Richard Hannon before being shipped abroad, winning four more races and posting an RPR of 101. Owner Mrs. Victoria Machen is 5/32 but has tasted 2-year-old success with Lions House, who won the first two races on AW as a 2-year-old for Roger Varian in 2023, and Empress Matilda, who is 1/1 winning on 2-year-old debut in 2024 again for Roger Varian. Trainer Marco Botti also targets this meeting with 2-year-olds, with 15/88 wins since 2012, showing a healthy LSP of £83.20 if ridden by a professional jockey (no claiming apprentice).
I Maximus has won in the all-weather over 6 furlongs. More recently at Windsor, he finished fifth over 6 furlongs on good to firm ground. He will wear cheekpieces for the first time.

Stayed on really well in the closing stages when a beaten favourite at Lingfield and probably went into many trackers as he didn't get a clear run. Runs off the same mark of 71 and can be in the mix again at a generous price of 5/1.
Shaped nicely LTO here over 5f, staying on nicely at the finish in 4th. Now back to 6f and 1lb below last winning mark here last summer.

I’m backing Priapos, the progressive 3-year-old Zoustar gelding trained by Ralph Beckett, in tomorrow’s Jockey Club Partner Handicap (6f, Class 4). He arrives in good heart after a solid reappearance effort??'finishing a respectable 3rd of 16 in a competitive Ascot handicap on May 9 under Rossa Ryan, beaten just 1½ lengths and showing a sharp turn of foot. He then busied up in the Royal Ascot Betting With World Pool Handicap at Goodwood on June 13, finishing 8th of 10, but that run on fast turf will likely have sharpened him up for this easier contest.
Priapos is entered here with Rossa Ryan again in the plate??'no stranger to big-field tactics??'and his promising Ascot run proves he handles track and trip. Rated around 79, he looks well treated and has shown he stays close to the pace in strong company.

The 5yo had 2 wins from 7 last year and some near misses - not beaten far in a couple of higher grade races. His two runs this year should have him right for this handicap - not having a clear run last time out. On a handy looking mark and William Buick takes over in the saddle.

Dashing Dick has an excellent record at the July Course and looks interesting back there in this Class 4 handicap. He has 4 career wins, with the last 2 coming here in August '23 and July '24. The last was off a mark of 73, and having looked like returning to form when second at Yarmouth off 76 last month, a 1lb rise might not stop him. He looks a good EW bet at these odds.
Much improved performance LTO when 4th of 10 at Chester last month, and mark remains unchanged, which provides an opportunity to build on that effort.

Despite this containing some potential 3yo improvers, FISCAL POLICY looks a big price for a sort that is very used to winning and still looks to be fairly well handicapped on the current turf mark. Stable have been great to follow of late too and I wouldn't be surprised if this one outruns this price. There's a chance some of the younger ones improve but this one should still give its running.
Already has a win to her name at listed level, so the rest of the field shall have to up their game to get past this one today.

Rossa Ryan rode Amberia to an impressive six length win making all over seven furlongs at Leicester earlier this month in her first race. She drops in distance here and the Leicester race was a restricted maiden for band D two year olds but she is still obviously talented and could go close here.
Won a Hamilton maiden on the second run when well fancied. This looks harder but should have a good chance of going on again.

Well overpriced to me, as was a good second to subsequent Albany Stakes winner at Royal Ascot last time when they met at Carlisle. On a line through Fitzella, has the beating of Bella Lyra, who was behind that one on debut, and Fitzella also went on to be fourth in the Albany. Stepping up to 6f should suit, as has run four times on stiff tracks over 5f and stays on well. Bella Lyra won at Windsor in a novice fillies race last time, and last year's winner of this, Celandine, did the same thing, so is respected. But my fancy looks underestimated here, as had the form in the book and promises to stay.
Meelaf was not far away when fourth in a G3 in France last week and could improve today back with the fillies in listed company.

A beaten favourite over course and distance in an apprentice here just 5 days ago. Turned round quickly for this race, remains on the same mark but could benefit from the more experienced hands of Silvestre De Sousa in the saddle and the first time visor could offer improvement too.

Orange Sky likes it here at Newcastle, both winning and placing on previous runs, and stands a very good chance of winning again if breaking well. Top yard and jockey that have a decent strike rate. E/W prospect.

Salve Electra showed vastly improved form on her first run on turf when getting up to win by a nose at Brighton. The handicapper's mark of 69 looks fair as the horse she beat, getting twelve pounds, Immediate Effect, is rated 81. She may have to improve again to win but should be involved in the finish.

Dereham won this race in both 2022 off 58 and 2023 off 57. He was not so good last year on good to firm when only 5th of 6 off 58. But even as a nine-year-old, he started the season okay, finishing 2nd of 9 at Yarmouth off 52, and he retains that lowly mark here with Saffie Osborne on board.

Three runs for the 4yo this year, three near misses in quality big field handicap races, including £31K and £52K contests. Same mark for this £10K handicap, suited by the quick ground and Ryan Moore taking over in the saddle.

Only 2-22, but those wins came in a novice on the Rowley Mile when with Paul and Oliver Cole, and a hot Galway handicap last summer when with Micky Fenton. Now in the hands of Pam Sly and has run really well with placed efforts here and at Chelmsford the last twice. Should be bang there once again this afternoon.
Cogitate came good last time to win easily over a mile after a fair show at this course previously. Only last-time-out winner on show and can prove value Each Way at current odds.

Kept on inside the final furlong when 3rd of 15 over a mile on the Chelmsford Tapeta last time out. Will welcome the drop in trip, being a winner over this trip on the Rowley course here in the race prior to that.

Tennessee Gold won 3 times last season and ran okay on debut this year when 12th at Chelmsford on 1st June. He was denied a clear run there but should find improvement. Off the same mark, he looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

CRACKING GOLD has yet to fire on the flat but is showing signs of getting there with a decent run from a high draw at Chester. That was in a much tougher race than this assignment, and with a decent looking run at Newmarket last season to his name, I think he lands a race on the flat before too long. Hopefully gets close regardless.

Saffie Osborne weaved her way through to win on Hickory over 7f at Ascot first time out this season off 86. His best form recently has been restricted to Ascot. But although a seven-year-old and trained at Newmarket by James Fanshawe until this May, he has yet to run at Newmarket on either course and could be suited to it. He had an interrupted early career, winning his only two-year-old race over 7f at Yarmouth, then did not run as a three-year-old and then won his next two races as a four-year-old over 7f at Kempton in October and December 2022. He has often run well in big field handicaps on a straight course and should go close off a mark of 90.

Royal Velvet is a lightly raced four-year-old filly from the W J Knight yard, carrying a low weight and showing recent winning form. She returns to suitable conditions and remains unexposed in handicaps. With improving form and generous odds, she’s a strong each-way contender and a lively outside chance.

Small each-way tip for Aramis Grey who is having her first run at this course but she has run well at similar types of tracks so that offers some hope of a good run today. Slightly below form over 6f last time out, held up in rear and then made some progress in the second half of that race , now moves back up in trip by 1f which does look more suitable. Still on what looks like a fair rating and the draw isn't too bad, drawn in Stall number 1.

Today’s top bet at Newcastle is Godwinson in the 3:45. Trained by W J Haggas and ridden by Tom Marquand, he won last time out and looks well-handicapped in this Class 2 race. Proven at the trip, supported in the market, and from a top stable, he’s primed to follow up with another strong performance.

Virtually no pace on here at all except Superposition and Local Hero. You'd think that anything coming from further back will struggle here. Godwinson, whilst likely still improving, won't be able to come from the back like he did in the Lincoln and is up in the weights as a result of that. That form has taken knocks regardless. I do like Tribal Chief, and it's possible a change of tactics and back down in trip he could simply be too good. But like the favorite, if he tries to come from behind, as has done previously, he'll likely struggle. Boiling Point on first run of the season off top weight and couldn't be backing. Superposition has won twice on the AW previously, making the running once and sitting prominent the other. Went wrong last time on turf, gelding lost his action, but nothing prominent there did overly well anyway, so likely expended too much early. Would imagine will try to make all here and will be hard to peg back.

Boiling Point did not do much last year, but all the runs were in good company, including a listed win. He ended that year with a couple of decent G3 runs, managing a fourth in the last race. He returns today running for a new yard with a drop to C2 and could come straight in with a bang.

Has C&D form and is just 2 lbs above last winning mark. Has been competing respectably in class 2 handicaps and was a good 2nd here earlier in the year behind the progressive Storm Star from this mark.

Ron O made his stable debut at York a fortnight ago. He placed 6th of 12 that day but that was after an absence of 258 days. He did well when with Ray Craggs and having had the benefit of that recent run could bounce back.

The 6-year-old has two 8f C/D wins from his last six starts. Decent run over the C/D when last seen, on Championship Finals Day, not having a great track position in the race. Slightly lower mark now, this race is not as strong, and he will be fresh after a 10-week break.

Back down to a winning mark of 92, having won the Lincoln over this trip and off this mark in 2024. Struggled in 4 subsequent races off higher marks but only beaten 3.5 lengths when 5th of 10 over the extended mile at Epsom off a mark of 94 last time out and could go well off this mark dropping in trip.

Stable coming back into form, and this horse won 3 on the bounce at the back end of last season. Shaped nicely at Epsom on the comeback from this mark when 7th in the Nifty Stakes Handicap. Has form on the AW, and the progression could continue here with a good draw.

Penzance comes into today after three midfield runs on turf, which had dropped him back to his last AW winning mark. Although most of his wins have been on Poly, he does have a win here under his belt from early last year and is worth a chance with the top draw.

I'm backing Fantasy Believer, the evergreen 8-year-old Make Believe gelding trained by Ed Walker, in tomorrow’s JenningsBet In Belmont Handicap over 1 m 2f 42y on Newcastle’s Tapeta. He returns from a break of over 160 days off a mark of 90 and was last seen finishing fifth of nine at this track and trip back in January??'his first run after a layoff??'showing he handles the surface and the forecast fast pace well .
That seasonal return at Newcastle reads well, considering he clocked a Timeform rating of 83 and was only beaten a few lengths??'he’s clearly tightened up since then. With Tom Marquand booked for the ride and Newcastle being one of the few tracks where his form is consistent, he could bounce back strongly, especially in this 11-runner class 2 field, where a strong tripper can capitalise. At likely odds of around 10/1, he offers appealing each-way appeal given his proven ability to race prominently on Tapeta and grind it out late.

A course and distance winner off a mark of 80 in May 2024, races off 78 here but with Amie Waugh in the saddle claiming 3 pounds, is effectively 5 pounds below that winning mark. Didn’t stay the trip over 3 furlongs further last time out and bled from the nose. The drop back to this trip and off this mark appeal.
Only had four runs to date, the best of them being last time out on handicap debut. This could well build on that, back up in trip.

Lightly raced 3-year-old filly. Something was amiss in her two runs this year - on turf last time out. She was a good runner-up on her handicap debut during December on this surface in a much stronger handicap than this contest. She has a 6lb lower mark now. A six-week break and a return to this surface could see her bounce back.
Went agonizingly close in a 12K race last time at Chester, and this does look a little easier. So a repeat of that run should see him win today.

Singarda is a 2-year-old gelding trained by Tony Coyle. Kaine Wood has an unusual pedigree line as there isn't much to go on. Sired by Zoustar, a four-time Group winner over 6-7 furlongs in Australia, and out of an unraced dam sired by Frankel, but no apparent dam listed for her. One interesting thing is Singarda is entered in the William Hill Two Year Old Trophy (Listed Race) in October. So this 10,000 guineas purchase may have been showing a bit at home, and Kevin Stott looks like a significant jockey booking, holding a 100% record on 2-year-olds in maidens Eye Up Its Maggie.

I'm Next is in stall number 8, which is a decent draw for his racing style. He tends to race mid-division or towards the rear, and on this 7f AW trip, the draw should not compromise his chances of getting a good position early. Trained by T D Easterby with Sean Kirrane up, he has a 20% win rate at this distance and some solid placed efforts in this class. Beaten 8 lengths last time but was in good form before. Needs to improve on AW but has an each-way chance. Pace should be good for him from this draw.

Ziggy's Triton came 2nd by a head last time out and has placed twice in its 3 starts. Tom Marquand takes the ride, and I'm expecting another big run. Tom has a good strike rate on the all-weather and has every chance if getting a decent break out. Distance is ideal. E/W prospect.
Ann Terry has won once over 6 furlongs. Last month, she finished last out of 9 horses in Thirsk over 6 furlongs on good ground. Prior to this, she was in good form.
Narrowly beaten runner-up at Musselburgh earlier this month and can go one better here off an only 2 lbs higher mark.

Crownthorpe is a well-handicapped outsider in Race 7 at Newcastle, trading around 7.50. Once rated much higher, he’s now on a career-low mark. Despite modest recent form, he’s a proven performer at the trip and class. With any spark of old ability, he could outrun his odds at value.

HEREKIOS best run of the year was when last seen over this trip in March and that came from three pounds higher in the handicap. I think he's worthy of consideration back down in trip and returning to a potentially favoured track. Maiden status still a niggle but there's a definite each-way chance.

4th at Chester first time out hints at bigger and better things to come today. I think he can improve in form, and 6f will suit this horse's running and speed. His trainer is a specialist at Newcastle, and I think he can get the best out of him.
4th on debut in a Ripon novice was an acceptable start. Should come on bundles for that run and is definitely my idea of the winner.
Ibn Altheeb was an OK second on debut last week in C4 and drops to C5 today. Worth a chance that he gets on with the AW, as he should be all the better for that first run.
Irish Dancer is looking strong in what looks like a weak enough race on paper. Should get the job done for us.
Returned to form with a decent third place over course and distance last time. Though this is the same class as that race, to me it looks a little easier, so should go close.
Rainwater gained its first turf win on its eleventh start. It has a 3lb claimer on board today. If in the same form again here, it should land this, and the form of the last win has taken a boost.

Renesmee is in stall number 4, a fairly useful draw for this 8f trip. Trained by Michael Keady with K S McHugh riding, she has a modest 10% win rate over this distance but has been consistent with 4 places on similar going. Down in trip today after running to form over 10f at Leicester last time, just beaten 3 lengths off a 65 mark. Down to 64 today with cheekpieces on (with a decent record in them) also, so on balance, she looks the pick here.

Snow Berry was winning for the 8th time in her career when winning over 5 furlongs here at Nottingham two weeks ago. She steps up to 6 furlongs here, but she won over course and distance in 2021, and off just 1lb higher than her highest winning mark, she can go in again.
The favorite Itraaq may well hover up but is going to have to improve considerably on what she's shown so far. My selection has, I think, the stronger form credentials.
Trainer James Owen has a great record with his 3-year-olds in flats in the UK so far this season, with no fewer than 9 winners from just 48 outings for a win percentage of 19%.
Dual course and distance winner last season who returned with a good effort at Doncaster before a below par effort here last time. Needs to put that behind her but should run well if doing so.
Has won at this course, which counts for a lot, but has been guilty of being a bit unreliable. However, it will look to be competitive now back on the flats after a couple of runs on the jump.
Pomme Pomme is in excellent form with 5 wins in the past 5 races, he won by 2 lengths at Haydock just 5 days ago and he ca win again today in this small field here at Hamilton.
Promising start to handicapping, finishing 2 1/4 lengths off the winner, who is now rated 81. Word of Mouth runs off 71 here and looks absolutely suited to this drop in trip.

This H Bethell-trained 3-year-old gelding has won twice over six furlongs and placed second over seven furlongs in his last three races on good to soft ground. The latest was at Carlisle 10 days ago when going clear inside the final furlong to beat the D Thompson-trained Stormy Pearl by 3 1/2 lengths. With D Tudhope back onboard, he can defy his six-pound penalty and follow up tonight.

Drops a couple of pounds and down in class and grade. This is a big opportunity for him in a 0-62, the lowest grade he has raced in since winning a 0-65 last year. Back down to his preferred trip after disappointing over 7f last time.

This B Ellison-trained filly made a promising racecourse debut over five furlongs on good to soft ground at Carlisle 27 days ago. She stayed on strongly in the closing stages to only be beaten 1/2 in third of the nine runners behind the well-backed A M Balding-trained Sands Of Spain. With the stiff uphill finish here in her favor, she looks hard to oppose under Callum Rodriguez.
Close at the head of the market, but this one may just have a bit more quality about him judged by past performances and had a nice pipe opener last time.

Billy No Mates could be about to strike with a solid effort last time out at Carlisle. He hasn't won in a while but is some 10lb lower than his last winning Official Rating. The fourth home that day has boosted that form and he has definite claims here.

Getting to the last chance saloon here. Promising reappearance 3 runs back but has not advanced his form from last year's levels. He drops in class here, back into a class 3, and drops another pound, so is now a pound lower than his last winning mark less than a year ago.

Three runs this year and the 4yo is progressing nicely. A cosy 2L winner two starts back. He was a close 4th of 13 four weeks ago in a useful £34K handicap - drawn on the wrong side. Facing much lower rated rivals now, strong jockey booking, big chance.
Brooklyn Nine Nine finished well into a close second to Bergerac over course and distance 11 days ago. It is due to go back up two pounds in the future and should go close again.
Bethell and Rodriguez are having a fine season, and this one had a nice seasonal bow at Carlisle last time. Any improvement on that run should see him go close here.
Form figures are nothing special, but it is down a class here and on top weight. So, if returning to form, it is the class act here. Jockey booking is a positive.

Jack Of Clubs was far too keen first time out this season at Carlisle and weakened away well before the finish over five furlongs. But he is back to a mark of 55, the same mark at which he won last July at Beverley, and he could go close in this selling handicap.

Built on a solid debut when 2nd at Bath last time out over 5.5f, shaping even better than the bare result. Comes here with more experience than most of the principals and the pick of form. Will take all the beating.

Emerald Army is in stall number 5, a decent draw for a 7f trip. Trained by David Carroll with Zak Wheatley aboard, he has run 20 times with a 20% win rate and 40% place rate. He won narrowly off a 54 mark over 6f at Thirsk in April. His latest run was a bit below par, finishing fifth beaten 5 lengths off a 60 mark, but stepping back up in trip to 7f should suit him better today. In good hands and with a positive pace likely he should be right about there.
Petra Celera was a LTO winner on the all-weather. Makes a return to turf tonight carrying a 5lb penalty. Has winning claims again with winning apprentice jockey Jack Nicholls back on board.

Cooperation was ridden by Elizabeth Gale last week at Redcar. In hindsight, she made too much use of him in the early part of the race. After being headed in the final furlong, he lost several places late on, finishing 5th of 9, a length behind Monsieur Fantaisie in 3rd. He could reverse that result at Leicester if not leading until late on this time.
I expect this horse to run a good race and get the job done. At 4/1, it just can't be ignored.

Just five career runs for the 3yo filly. Much improved for her last two runs after switching to turf. Runner-up twice and now facing much lower-rated rivals than what she faced five weeks ago - the winner boosting the form and rated 13lb higher now. Room for improvement and running off the same mark as her last handicap.

Three On Thursday has only had four runs. The first three on the all-weather were not too bad, and last time on turf in her first handicap, she finished six lengths 3rd of 10 off 59 and could get at least placed again off 58.
Only 1-13 and yet to win a handicap but has run well in a couple of starts at Pontefract and Hamilton so far this season. Should be capable of striking soon.

Two runs for the 8yo this year, going close two weeks ago and he should be sharper now. He was a close 3rd of 11 that day, starting slowly but finishing fast, posting a high RPR rating. Lower mark and much lower rated rivals in this handicap.

LEVEL UP looks to be running well, and the run from this mark last time out suggests there's still more to offer. Connections seem to be capitalizing on a promising streak, and he should be there or thereabouts once again.

A few runs over hurdles for the 6yo mare but just four flat runs. She was just a head behind the runner-up on the AW four weeks ago over this 12f trip. Decent RPR rating posted. She’s facing much lower-rated rivals in this turf handicap.
Four times a winner over this trip on Tapeta and of interest trying this trip for the first time on the flat on second start for new yard.

Regally Blonde joined Ben Case from Alan Oliver in Ireland in December 2022. She had been a fair performer on the flat at around 12f. After initially hurdling in the UK, she was rated 73 for her first flat race at Lingfield in October 2023. She has dropped sharply to 53 after not many flat races, but her latest at Windsor this month, when 4th of 11 beaten only two and a quarter lengths off 54, was not too bad.
Having a torrid time, similar to my current form this month. The last win last summer seems ages ago, but it helps that he's won off a higher mark and conditions are ideal for him tomorrow.
Came good last time at Ripon, and with the stable returning to some form of late, no reason why she can't follow up off top weight here.

Gelded son of Wootton Bassett & Beyond Limits ( Dam's sire Zoffany ) who was last seen at Kempton 72 days ago where finishing 8th/10 however this is no horse to underestimate as he arrives here in top nick operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 59 and is most certainly open to plenty of progress and Charlie Johnston's inmate is capable of much better than his current operating mark especially now as a 3yo and can begin to trouble the judge of this sort of mark steps up in trip here racing over the 1 mile trip for the first time that being a positive move by his connections as this new trip can bring out further improvement and Optimatum will highly appreciate this step up in trip and worth noting trainer Charlie Johnston has a healthy £42.05 profit to a £1 level stake with horses being stepped up in trip this is the perfect assignment for Optimatum to showcase a much better piece of form jockey S D Bowen takes the ride and can give Optimatum a promising ride here at Leicester must be taken seriously and accordingly and by no means underestimated here . Respected .
No wins yet from 11 runs, but I think a switch back to turf might be beneficial for him despite the mark being unchanged. Also, hoping the tongue strap back on does the trick.
